{{Pizza}}

[[Pizza]] is a staple of [[Italian cuisine]]. It has become one of the most recognizable and popular dishes worldwide. Its widespread adoption into other cuisines, replacing the local traditional dishes, is traced to the early 20th century.

==Europe==

===Italy===
[[File:Eq it-na pizza-margherita sep2005 sml.jpg|thumb|[[Pizza Margherita]]]]
[[File:Pizza al taglio.jpg|thumb|''[[Pizza al taglio]]'' in [[Rome]], Italy]]
[[File:Pizza Quattro Stagioni.jpg|thumb|[[Pizza quattro stagioni]]]]

Authentic ''[[Neapolitan pizza|pizze napoletane]]'' ('Neapolitan pizzas') are typically made with tomatoes and [[Mozzarella|mozzarella cheese]]. They can be made with ingredients such as [[San Marzano tomato]]es, which grow on the volcanic plains to the south of [[Mount Vesuvius]], and fiordilatte mozzarella made with cow's milk.

According to the rules proposed by the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pizzanapoletana.org/index_eng.php |title=''Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana'' |website=Pizzanapoletana.org |access-date=7 July 2012}}</ref> the genuine Neapolitan pizza dough consists of wheat flour (type 0 or 00, or a mixture of both), natural Neapolitan yeast or brewer's yeast, salt and water. For proper results, strong flour with high protein content (as used for bread-making rather than cakes) must be used. The dough must be kneaded by hand or with a low-speed mixer. After the rising process, the dough must be formed by hand without the help of a rolling pin or other machine, and may be no more than {{convert|3|mm|in|abbr=on|sp=us}} thick. The pizza must be baked for 60–90 seconds in a {{convert|485|C}} stone oven with an oak-wood fire.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fornobravo.com/vera_pizza_napoletana/VPN_spec.html|title=Vera Pizza Napoletana Specification | Verace Pizza Napoletana |website=Fornobravo.com |date=24 May 2004 |access-date=2 April 2009}}</ref> When cooked, it should be crispy, tender and fragrant. There are three official variants:
* [[pizza marinara]], which is made with tomato, garlic, oregano and extra-virgin olive oil,
* [[pizza Margherita]], made with tomato, sliced mozzarella, basil and [[extra-virgin olive oil]], and
* ''pizza Margherita di bufala'' made with tomato, sliced [[buffalo mozzarella]] from [[Campania]], basil and [[Olive oil|extra-virgin olive oil]].
''Pizza napoletana'' is a [[traditional speciality guaranteed]] (TSG) product in Europe.<ref>{{cite news |title=Naples pizza makers celebrate EU trademark status |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/8499611.stm |publisher=BBC News |date=4 February 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=Publication of an application pursuant to Article 8(2) of Council Regulation (EC) No 509/2006 on agricultural products and foodstuffs as traditional specialties guaranteed – Pizza napoletana (2008/C 40/08) |url=http://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=OJ:C:2008:040:0017:0025:EN:PDF |magazine=Official Journal of the European Union |date=14 February 2009}}</ref>

[[Roman pizza]], as well as pizza in many other parts of Italy, is available in two different styles. Take-away shops sell ''pizza rustica'' or ''[[pizza al taglio]]''.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/isbn_9781741798562 |url-access=registration |quote=Lazio, pizza al taglio. |title=Lonely Planet Rome |author1=Duncan Garwood |author2=Abigail Hole |publisher=Lonely Planet |date=1 May 2012 |isbn=9781742208428 |access-date=4 July 2013}}</ref> This pizza is cooked in long, rectangular baking pans and relatively thick ({{Convert|1-2|cm|in|1|abbr=on}}). The pizza is often cooked in an [[Electric stove|electric oven]]. It is usually cut with scissors or a knife and sold by weight. In [[pizzeria]]s, pizza is served in a dish in its traditional round shape. It has a thin, crisp base quite different from the thicker and softer Neapolitan-style base. It is usually cooked in a [[Oven|wood-fired oven]], giving the pizza its unique flavor and texture. In Rome, a ''pizza napoletana'' is topped with tomato, mozzarella, anchovies, oregano, capers and oil (thus, what in [[Naples]] is called ''pizza romana'', in Rome is called ''pizza napoletana''). Other types of Lazio-style pizza include:
* [[Pizza capricciosa]]
* [[Pizza quattro formaggi]]
* [[Pizza quattro stagioni]]
* [[Pizza Rossini]]
* [[Pizzetta]]
* [[Sicilian pizza]] 

====Legislation for traditional Italian pizza====
There was a bill before the [[Italian Parliament]] in 2002 to safeguard the traditional Italian pizza,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.senato.it/japp/bgt/showdoc/showText?tipodoc=Ddlpres&leg=13&id=00007353&offset=4504&length=6529 |title=Bill for traditional Italian pizza |publisher=Senato.it |access-date=2 April 2009}}</ref> specifying permissible ingredients and methods of processing<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.senato.it/leg/13/BGT/Schede/Ddliter/testi/13214_testi.htm |title=Permissible ingredients and methods of processing |publisher=Senato.it |access-date=2 April 2009}}</ref> (e.g., excluding frozen pizzas). Only pizzas which followed these guidelines could be called "traditional Italian pizzas" in Italy. On 9 December 2009, the [[European Union]], upon Italian request, granted traditional speciality guaranteed safeguard to traditional Neapolitan pizza, in particular to "Margherita" and "Marinara".<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110715092118/http://www.pizzamarketplace.com/article/96776/EU-grants-Neapolitan-pizza-Traditional-Specialty-Guaranteed-label EU grants Neapolitan pizza Traditional Specialty Guaranteed label], Pizza Marketplace</ref> The European Union enacted a [[protected designation of origin]] system in the 1990s.

===Finland===	
Poro, formerly known as the Berlusconi pizza, is [[Kotipizza]]'s product name for a pizza with smoked [[reindeer]] meat, tomato sauce, cheese, [[Chanterelle|chanterelle mushrooms]] and red onion.<ref>{{cite web |title=Berlusconi |url=https://www.kotipizza.fi/tuotteet/pizzat/berlusconi |language=fi |access-date=29 August 2019 }}</ref>

With Pizza Berlusconi, Kotipizza won the America's Plate International pizza contest in [[New York City]] in March 2008, beating the [[Italian-American]]s, who came in second place, and the [[Australia]]ns in third.<ref>{{cite web |author=Anneli Hertsi |date=15 June 2008 |title=Berlusconi-pizza kerää mainetta Italiassa |trans-title=Berlusconi Pizza gains fame in Italy |url=http://www.kauppalehti.fi/5/i/talous/uutiset/etusivu/uutinen.jsp?oid=12605&ext=rss |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120329165745/http://www.kauppalehti.fi/5/i/talous/uutiset/etusivu/uutinen.jsp?oid=12605&ext=rss |archivedate=March 29, 2012 |website=[[Kauppalehti]] |language=fi}}</ref>

===Hungary===
Hungarians enjoy most of the traditional pizza toppings, but there are some unique local varieties, including "Magyaros" ("Hungarian-style") pizza, which usually has toppings such as bacon, ''kolbász'' ([[Hungarian sausages|Hungarian sausage]]), salami, hot peppers, and red onion.<ref>{{cite web |date= |title=Magyaros pizza receptet keresel? | Nosalty |url=https://www.nosalty.hu/receptek/kategoria/pizza/magyaros-pizza |accessdate=2022-03-27 |publisher=Nosalty.hu}}</ref> "White pizza" (see below) is also popular, especially because it is similar to Hungarian [[Lángos|''kenyérlángos'' or ''langalló'']] (a type of flatbread often topped with sour cream, bacon and onions).<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 January 2020 |title=Taste Hungary! – Recipe of the irresistible Hungarian pizza "Langalló" |url=https://dailynewshungary.com/taste-hungary-recipe-of-the-irresistible-hungarian-pizza-kenyerlangos/}}</ref>

===Iceland===
While Iceland has many traditional American and Italian style pizza toppings, [[banana]]s are a common topping in the country.<ref name="Thornhill, Jan 2010" />

===Norway===
Norwegians eat the most pizza in the world according to a 2004 survey by [[ACNielsen]] 2004, 5.4 kg/year per capita. 50 million frozen pizzas were sold that year, with consumption being 22,000 [[ton]]s of frozen pizza, 15,000 tons of home-baked and 13,000 tons of restaurant-made pizzas.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wahlberg |first1=Maria |url=http://www.svd.se/naringsliv/norrmannen-varldsbast-pa-att-ata-pizza_1042389.svd|title=Svenska dagbladet: Pizza statistics according to AC Nielsen|work=SvD.se|date=13 January 2005|access-date=4 October 2014}}</ref>

===Poland===
According to thefirstnews.com, "...most ordered pizza in Poland is the [[Pizza capricciosa|capricciosa]], while the favourite toppings in Poland are ham, salami, mushrooms, onions and bacon. [[Garlic mayonnaise|Garlic dipping sauce]] is the favourite choice to accompany a pizza is with 68 percent choosing this and tomato sauce in second place with 14 percent."<ref>{{cite web |title=It's pan-tastic: pizza more popular in Poland than in Italy as order-in food |url=https://www.thefirstnews.com/article/its-pan-tastic-pizza-more-popular-in-poland-than-in-italy-as-order-in-food-1039 |website=www.thefirstnews.com |date=February 10, 2020 |access-date=6 December 2021 |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200813200617/https://www.thefirstnews.com/article/its-pan-tastic-pizza-more-popular-in-poland-than-in-italy-as-order-in-food-10397 |archive-date=13 August 2020}}</ref>

=== Slovenia ===
Pizza was introduced to Slovenia in the 1970s. The country's first pizzeria, Pizzeria Parma in Ljubljana, opened in 1974.<ref>{{cite web |title=Danes je svetovni dan pice |url=https://www.rtvslo.si/enostavno/pomembni-dnevi/danes-je-svetovni-dan-pice/657254 |website=RTV Slovenija |date=9 February 2023 |language=sl |access-date=26 July 2026}}</ref> It became known for a distinctive thick-crust style of pizza with generous toppings, baked in a signature conveyor-belt oven.<ref>{{cite web |title=Parma v Maxiju že 50 let |url=https://odprtakuhinja.delo.si/brbotanje/obisk/parma-v-maxiju-ze-50-let |website=Odprta kuhinja |publisher=Delo |language=sl |access-date=26 July 2026}}</ref> One of its best-known varieties is topped with ham, mushrooms, cheese, and an egg.
===Sweden===
The first pizza to be served in Sweden was in 1947 at the [[ASEA]] staff canteen in [[Västerås]] but it was not until 1968 that it became available to the general public at the Stockholm restaurant Östergök.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Nilsson|first=Magnus|title=The Nordic Cook Book|publisher=Phaidon|year=2015|isbn=9780714868721|location=London|page=476}}</ref>

One Swedish speciality is the ''calskrove'', a calzone-type pizza containing [[hamburger]]s and fries. This type of pizza became popular in Sweden in 2007.<ref>[https://www.aftonbladet.se/a/G15dA6 7 superpizzor som förändrade Sverige], ''[[Aftonbladet]]'' 1 January 2016. Accessed on 3 July 2023.</ref> Some pizzas in Sweden can have unconventional toppings such as [[pineapple]] or [[banana]] (usually in combination with [[curry sauce]]). In 2019 a special type of pizza in [[Skottorp]] achieved international fame when its toppings included [[kiwifruit]].<ref>[https://www.expressen.se/kvallsposten/stellans-pizza-blev-en-snackis-i-hela-varlden/ Stellans kiwi-pizza har blivit en snackis i hela världen], ''[[Expressen]]'' 15 January 2020. Accessed on 3 July 2023.</ref>

==Asia==

===South and East Asia===

====China====
{{Main|Pizza in China}}
The presence of pizza [[restaurant chain]]s in China has contributed to a significant increase in pizza consumption in the country.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8OfIBgAAQBAJ&pg=PT175|title=Fat China: How Expanding Waistlines are Changing a Nation|last1=French|first1=Paul|last2=Crabbe|first2=Matthew|date=1 July 2010|publisher=Anthem Press|isbn=9780857288035|language=en}}</ref> [[Pizza Hut]] opened its first store in China in 1990,<ref>Smith, A.F. (2012). ''[https://books.google.com/books?id=Wq3tvL_uIHcC Fast Food and Junk Food: An Encyclopedia of What We Love to Eat]''. Fast Food and Junk Food: An Encyclopedia of what We Love to Eat. ABC-CLIO. p. 121. {{ISBN|978-0-313-39393-8}}. Retrieved 16 July 2017. "In 1990 Pizza Hut was the first restaurant chain to introduce American pizza to China. It also localized its menu."</ref><ref name="Edwards 2011">{{cite web | last=Edwards | first=William | title=The Pros and Cons of Franchising in China | website=China Business Review | date=June 1, 2011 | url=http://www.chinabusinessreview.com/the-pros-and-cons-of-franchising-in-china/ | access-date=July 16, 2017}}</ref> and Pizza Hut and [[Domino's Pizza]] both expanded in the Chinese market in the 2000s.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chinabusinessreview.com/the-pros-and-cons-of-franchising-in-china/|title=The Pros and Cons of Franchising in China|date=1 July 2011|website=China Business Review|language=en-US|access-date=12 May 2019}}</ref> To fit with China's market demand and national culinary peculiarities Pizza Hut modified its pizza recipes to include local ingredients, such as [[Crab stick|crab sticks]], tuna, soy sauce and corn.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://you.stonybrook.edu/americanchinesefood/what-changes-have-they-made/|title=What changes have they made? {{!}} American Food in China|website=you.stonybrook.edu|access-date=12 May 2019}}</ref> As of 2019, Pizza Hut had over 2,000 outlets in China.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/03/05/business/kfc-fastfood-pizza-hut-china/index.html|title=Robot waiters and snail pizza: What US fast food brands do to please Chinese diners|author=Analysis by Daniel Shane|publisher=CNN|date=6 March 2019|access-date=12 May 2019}}</ref>

====India====
Pizza is an emerging fast food in India.<ref name="Kretzmann" /> Domestic pizza brands include U.S. Pizza, [[Smokin' Joes]] and [[Pizza Corner (restaurant)|Pizza Corner]]. Branded pizza is available in most cities in India. India is the largest market for [[Domino's Pizza]] outside the US. Pizza brands feature greater "recipe localization" from pizza makers than many other markets such as Latin America and Europe, but similar to other Asian pizza markets. Indian pizzas are generally spicier and more vegetable-oriented than those in other countries. For instance, oregano spice packs are included with a typical pizza order in India instead of Parmesan cheese.<ref name="Kretzmann">{{cite web|last=Kretzmann |first=David |url=http://www.fool.com/investing/general/2013/12/21/how-dominos-is-poised-to-benefit-from-india.aspx |title=How Domino's Is Poised to Benefit From India |publisher=Fool.com |date=21 December 2013 |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref> In addition to spicier and more vegetable-oriented ingredients, Indian pizza also utilizes unique toppings such as [[Ginger#Culinary|pickled ginger]].<ref name="Thornhill, Jan 2010">Thornhill, Jan. Who Wants Pizza?: The Kids' Guide to the History, Science & Culture of Food. Toronto: Maple Tree, 2010. Print.</ref>

====Indonesia====
In [[Indonesia]], [[Pizza Hut]] is the largest pizza chain restaurant, first entering Indonesia in 1984,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pizzahut.co.id/|title=About Pizza Hut | Pizza Hut|website=www.pizzahut.co.id}}</ref> followed by [[Domino's]] and Papa Ron's Pizza.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://paparonspizza.com/|title=PAPA RONS PIZZA | taste the difference!}}</ref> 

However, there are also Asian [[Eastern world|Eastern]] pizzas which includes Indonesian [[Fusion cuisine|fusion]] pizza that combine [[Indonesian cuisine|Indonesian favourite]] as pizza toppings – such as [[satay]],<ref name="Tempo-pizza">{{cite news |newspaper=Tempo.co |title=Beef Satay Pizza of Blue Jasmine |date=20 January 2015 |url=https://en.tempo.co/read/news/2015/01/20/199636148/Beef-Satay-Pizza-of-Blue-Jasmine}}</ref> [[Balado (food)|balado]] and [[rendang]].<ref name="JP-pizza">{{cite news |title=Seven pizzas that are more Indonesian than Italian |newspaper=The Jakarta Post |date=10 February 2017 |url=http://www.thejakartapost.com/life/2017/02/10/seven-pizzas-that-are-more-indonesian-than-italian.html}}</ref>
* ''Balado pizza'', spicy hot [[Balado (food)|balado]] chili pepper pizza, chicken or beef.<ref name="JP-pizza" />
* ''Rendang pizza'', spicy and savoury beef [[rendang]] pizza.<ref name="JP-pizza" />
* ''Satay pizza'', beef or chicken [[satay]] pizza with peanut sauce.<ref name="Tempo-pizza" />

====Japan====
American pizza chains entered [[Japan]] in the 1970s (e.g. [[Shakey's Pizza]] and Pizza Hut in 1973, Domino's in 1985). The largest Japanese pizza chain is [[Pizza-La]]. Local types of pizza are popular, with many using mayonnaise sauce, and sometimes other ingredients such as corn, potatoes, avocado, eel, or even honey or [[chocolate pizza]] (as a dessert). "Side orders" also often include items such as French fries, fried chicken, and baked pasta, as well as vegetable soups and green salads.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pizza-la.co.jp/sc_englishmenu.aspx|title=English Menu – 宅配ピザのピザーラ – PIZZA-LA|website=pizza-la.co.jp}}</ref>

One of the unique pizza toppings found in Japan is [[Squid as food|squid]]. While seafood may be found on pizzas in most markets worldwide to some extent, having squid as the focal ingredient is unique to Japan.<ref name="Thornhill, Jan 2010" />

Local crust variants also exist, for instance mochi pizza (crust made with Japanese [[mochi]] cakes).<ref>Ceccarini R. (2010) [http://icc.fla.sophia.ac.jp/global%20food%20papers/pdf/3_3_CECCARINI.pdf "Food Workers as Individual Agents of Culinary Globalization: Pizza and Pizza Chefs in Japan"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190819122832/http://icc.fla.sophia.ac.jp/global%20food%20papers/pdf/3_3_CECCARINI.pdf |date=19 August 2019 }}. Sophia University, Tokyo.</ref><ref>Ceccarini R. (2011) [http://www.brill.nl/pizza-and-pizza-chefs-japan-case-culinary-globalization ''Pizza and Pizza Chefs in Japan: A Case of Culinary Globalization'']. Brill Publishers, Netherlands.</ref>

====Korea====
Pizza is a popular food in [[South Korea]], especially among younger people.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-01-09 |title=The Weird and Wonderful World of Korean Pizza |url=https://roadsandkingdoms.com/2015/the-weird-and-wonderful-world-of-korean-pizza/ |access-date=2023-04-20 |website=Roads & Kingdoms |language=en-US}}</ref> 

[[North Korea]]'s first pizzeria opened in its capital [[Pyongyang]] in 2009.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/7945816.stm |publisher=BBC News |title=First North Korean pizzeria opens |date=16 March 2009 |access-date=22 May 2010}}</ref>

====Philippines====
Pizza first arrived in the Philippines during the American period (1901–1946). Many pizza restaurant chains that set up shop in the Philippines (e.g. [[Pizza Hut]], [[Domino's]], and [[Shakey's Pizza]]) are American in origin. The typical Filipino-style pizza is similar to Hawaiian pizza due to their usage of pineapple toppings, although sometimes instead of pepperoni, ham or hotdog chunks are used. There are also variants using traditional Filipino dishes such as sardines, dried [[tinapa]], [[bagnet]], and [[Vigan longganisa|longganisa]] as toppings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/food/375133/learn-about-the-history-of-the-pizza-on-national-pizza-day/story/|title=Learn about the history of the pizza on National Pizza Day|date=16 August 2014 }}</ref>

====Thailand====
The Pizza Company Thailand introduced [[durian]] pizza in 2018 to mixed reviews.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ooh or eww? The Pizza Company Thailand now serves durian pizza |work=Coconuts Bangkok |date=19 October 2018|url=https://coconuts.co/bangkok/news/ooh-eww-pizza-company-thailand-now-serves-durian-pizza/ |access-date=30 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Tuohy |first1=Laurel |title=Stinky Slices: We tried The Pizza Company's new Durian Pizza so you don't have to (VIDEO) |work=Coconuts Bangkok |date=2 November 2018 |url=https://coconuts.co/bangkok/food-drink/stinky-slices-tried-pizza-companys-new-durian-pizza-dont-video/ |access-date=30 April 2019}}</ref> Thailand also has many independent pizza restaurants, particularly in [[Bangkok]] and tourists areas. Pizza can range from chains serving American-style pizza with western or Thai toppings, to quite authentic Neapolitan and Roman style pizza in Bangkok.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.lifestyleasia.com/sg/dining/food/best-pizza-in-bangkok/ | title=13 places for the best pizzas in Bangkok today | date=12 June 2023 }}</ref>

==North America==

===Canada===
{{main|Pizza in Canada}}
There are several regional pizza varieties, with [[Windsor-style pizza]] from [[Windsor, Ontario]] being the most recognizable.

===Mexico===
{{redirect|Mexican pizza|the Taco Bell menu item|Mexican Pizza|the Oaxacan dish sometimes called "Mexican pizza"|Tlayuda}}
Pizza in Mexico is made with ingredients typical of [[Mexican cuisine]]. The usual toppings that can be found throughout Mexico are [[chorizo]], [[jalapeño]] chili peppers, grilled or fried onions, tomato, [[chili pepper]], [[shrimp]], [[avocado]], and sometimes beef, [[bell pepper]]s, [[tripas]], [[Tuna|canned tuna]] or [[scallop]]s. This pizza has the usual [[marinara sauce]] or white sauce and [[Mozzarella|mozzarella cheese]]. Variations, substituting [[Monterey Jack|Pepper Jack cheese]] or [[Oaxaca cheese]] for mozzarella, are also popular.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/fastfoodfix75ama0000alex |url-access=registration |quote=mexican pizza. |title=Fast Food Fix: 75+ Amazing Recipe Makeovers of Your Fast Food Restaurant Favorites |publisher=Rodale |first=Devin |last=Alexander |date=18 April 2006 |pages=[https://archive.org/details/fastfoodfix75ama0000alex/page/164 164]–165|isbn=9781594863103 |access-date=4 July 2013}}</ref>

===United States===
{{Main|Pizza in the United States}}

[[File:NYPizzaPie.jpg|thumb|[[New York–style pizza]]]]
[[File:Detroit Style Pizza from Calphalon Bread Pans.png|thumb|[[Detroit-style pizza]]]]

In 1905, the first pizza establishment in the United States was opened in [[New York City]]'s [[Little Italy, Manhattan|Little Italy]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Eric |last=Asimov |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/06/10/dining/new-york-pizza-the-real-thing-makes-a-comeback.html |title=New York Pizza, the Real Thing, Makes a Comeback |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=10 June 1998 |access-date=24 September 2006}}</ref> Due to the influx of Italian immigrants, the U.S. has developed regional forms of pizza, some bearing only a casual resemblance to the Italian original. However, virtually every suburb and city in the United States does have reasonably authentic Neapolitan-style pizza restaurants.<ref>[https://www.foodandwine.com/best-pizza-in-america-2024-8671677 Pizza in America] - [[Food & Wine|''Food and Wine'' magazine]]</ref>

The most renowned{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} pizza variety is [[New York–style pizza|New York-style pizza]], but other regional varieties include [[Detroit-style pizza|Detroit-style]], [[Chicago-style pizza|Chicago deep dish]], [[St. Louis–style pizza|St Louis-style]], [[California-style pizza|California-style]], [[Quad City–style pizza|Quad City-style]], [[Greek pizza|New England “Greek Style”]], [[New Haven-style pizza|New Haven-style]], [[Colorado-style pizza|Colorado mountain pie]], [[Minnesota-style pizza|Minneapolis-style]], [[Columbus-style pizza|Columbus-style]], [[Ohio Valley-style pizza|Ohio Valley-style]], [[Trenton tomato pie]], [[Brier Hill-style pizza|Briar Hill-style]], [[Altoona-style pizza|Altoona-style]], [[Dayton-style pizza|Dayton-style]],  and [[Beach pizza|Beach Pizza.]] 

The [[jumbo slice]] is an oversized New York–style pizza sold [[Pizza by the slice|by the slice]] to go, especially in the [[Adams Morgan]] neighborhood in [[Washington, D.C.]] The [[white clam pie]] is a pizza variety that originated at the [[Frank Pepe Pizzeria Napoletana]] restaurant in [[New Haven, Connecticut]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Barrett |first1=L. |last2=Abate |first2=L. |last3=Caporuscio |first3=R. |last4=Bello |first4=M. |last5=Bruno |first5=S. |title=Pizza, A Slice of American History |publisher=[[The Quarto Group|Voyageur Press]] |year=2014 |isbn=978-0-7603-4560-3 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vPCuBAAAQBAJ&pg=PA58 |page=58}}</ref> Barbecue pizza was first made at Coletta's in [[Memphis, Tennessee]], using pulled pork and barbecue sauce, now popular in the Southern United States. In [[California]], the barbecue chicken pizza is popular, first invented by [[Ed LaDou]] in 1985.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hungryhowies.com/blog/who-invented-bbq-chicken-pizza|title=Who Invented BBQ Chicken Pizza?|date=27 September 2017}}</ref>

==Oceania==

===Australia===
Australian variety of pizza named ''The Aussie'' (also called ''Aussie Bob'', ''Aussie Legend'', ''Aussie Bite'')<ref>{{cite web |url=https://aussiepizza.com.au |title=Aussie Pizza Raymond Terrace |access-date=2026-05-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.captainpizza.net.au/menu |title=Full Pizza Menu Online |website=Captain Pizza |access-date=2026-05-15}}</ref> features egg as a unique pizza topping, often paired with ham and bacon, and is attributed to Salvatore Della Bruna of [[Toto's Pizza House]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://lygonstreet.com.au/history-of-lygon-street/ |title=History of Lygon Street |website=LygonStreet.com.au |access-date=2026-05-15}}</ref> It has been served in restaurants around Australia, including [[Domino's Pizza Enterprises|Domino's]] in 1996 and 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://newsroom.dominos.com.au/blog/2020/9/30/a-slice-of-nostalgia-dominos-through-the-decades |title=A slice of nostalgia: Domino's through the decades |website=Domino's Newsroom |date=2020-09-30 |access-date=2026-05-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dominos.com.au/menu/pizzas/ |title=Domino's Pizza |date=2009-11-24 |access-date=2026-05-15 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091124210414/http://www.dominos.com.au/menu/pizzas/ |archive-date=2009-11-24}}</ref>

===New Zealand===
The usual Italian varieties are available and independent restaurants are common, coexisting with franchise chains. New Zealand's first dedicated pizza franchise was [[1974 in New Zealand#Events|opened]] by Pizza Hut in [[New Lynn]] in 1974, with [[Eagle Boys]] and [[Pizza Haven (Australia)|Pizza Haven]] following in the mid-1990s and Domino's in 2003.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/business/industries/77077227/the-evolution-of-new-zealands-pizza-industry |title=The evolution of New Zealand's pizza industry |author=Laura Walters |date=2016-03-04 |publisher=Stuff }}</ref> One notable indigenous chain is [[Hell Pizza]] established in 1996 – which now has outlets worldwide – distinguishing itself by often-controversial marketing and using only free-range ingredients. Furthermore, Middle-Eastern bakeries and kebabs shops often sell pizza, which is often done in [[List of pizza varieties by country#Turkey|Turkish style]].

In 2017, spaghetti pizza gained media attention when then [[Prime Minister of New Zealand]] [[Bill English]] posted a recipe to his [[Facebook]] account that included [[Canning|tinned]] spaghetti.<ref name="Canadian Broadcasting Corporation - 6 April 2017 - New Zealand PM divides nation by putting canned spaghetti on pizza">{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/radio/asithappens/as-it-happens-thursday-edition-1.4058508/new-zealand-pm-divides-nation-by-putting-canned-spaghetti-on-pizza-1.4058514|title=New Zealand PM divides nation by putting canned spaghetti on pizza|date=6 April 2017|work=As It Happens |publisher=[[CBC Radio]]|access-date=23 February 2019}}</ref> The recipe included [[Hawaiian pizza|pineapple as a topping]].<ref name="SBS World News - 6 April 2017 -New Zealand PM sparks outrage with his tinned spaghetti pizza">{{cite news|url=https://www.sbs.com.au/food/article/2017/04/06/new-zealand-pm-sparks-outrage-his-tinned-spaghetti-pizza|title=New Zealand PM sparks outrage with his tinned spaghetti pizza|date=6 April 2017|work=[[SBS World News]] |publisher=[[Special Broadcasting Service]] |access-date=1 March 2019}}</ref> Mixed responses on social media included support for spaghetti pizza as a simple and cheap family meal.<ref name="The Guardian - 6 April 2017 - Tinned spaghetti pizza: New Zealand's prime minister shocks with 'monstrous' recipe">{{cite news|last1=Roy|first1=Eleanor Ainge|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/apr/06/tinned-spaghetti-pizza-new-zealands-prime-minister-shocks-with-monstrous-recipe|title=Tinned spaghetti pizza: New Zealand's prime minister shocks with 'monstrous' recipe|date=6 April 2017|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=23 February 2019}}</ref> In 2019, Domino's included a "Hawaiian Spaghetti Pizza" on the menu on its franchises in [[New Zealand]].<ref name="New York Post - In 2007, [[São Paulo]] was the second largest consumer of pizza in the world, behind only New York City, with 1.4 million pizzas consumed daily. It also had 6,000 pizza establishments, out of a total of 25,000 in the country ({{percentage|6000|25000|2}}).<ref>{{cite web |last=Neves |first=Regina |date=10 July 2007 |title=São Paulo celebra o dia da pizza |trans-title=São Paulo celebrates pizza day |url=https://gazetamercantil.com/sao-paulo-celebra-o-dia-da-pizza |archive-url= |archive-date= |access-date=13 September 2023 |website=Gazeta Mercantil |language=pt-br}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.jb.com.br/economia/noticias/2007/08/27/sao-paulo-consome-mais-pizza-do-que-a-italia.html |title=São Paulo consome mais pizza do que a Itália |language=pt-br |trans-title=São Paulo consumes more pizza than Italy |first=Sérgio |last=Toledo |agency=InvestNews |website=[[Jornal do Brasil]] |date=27 August 2007 |access-date=5 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210906021143/https://www.jb.com.br/economia/noticias/2007/08/27/sao-paulo-consome-mais-pizza-do-que-a-italia.html |archive-date=6 September 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The date 10 July is "Pizza Day" in São Paulo, marking the final day of an annual competition among ''[[pizzaioli]]''. In São Paulo, almost every local neighborhood pizzeria uses wood-fired brick ovens.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scott |first=Jane |date=2023-02-20 |title=The Rise of Wood-Fired Pizzas: A Journey Through the History and Popularity of this Timeless Cooking Method |url=https://www.globalblogzone.com/wood-fired-pizzas-journey-through-history-and-timeless-cooking-method/ |access-date=2023-02-21 |website=Global Blog Zone |language=en-CA}}</ref>

Brazil is mostly liberal when it comes to pizza toppings. Apart from [[ketchup]], commonly added to pizzas by customers in some regions and sometimes frowned upon by foreigners,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uol.com.br/nossa/cozinha/noticias/redacao/2020/01/20/ketchup-na-pizza-e-o-assunto-do-momento-no-twitter-voce-aprova.htm |title=Ketchup na pizza volta a causar comoção no Twitter; de qual lado você está? |language=pt-br |trans-title=Ketchup on pizza creates Twitter commotion again; which side are you on? |website=[[Universo Online|UOL]] |date=20 January 2020 |access-date=6 September 2021}}</ref> Brazilian pizzas are sometimes very exotic, with choices such as chicken or [[beef Stroganoff]] pizza; [[cheeseburger]] pizza; [[French fries]] pizza; [[fettuccine]] pizza; among others.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://vejasp.abril.com.br/comida-bebida/pizza-combinacoes-inusitadas/ |title=Pizzas exóticas como as de cheeseburger, estrogonofe e feijoada |first1=Sophia |last1=Braun |first2=Victória |last2=Kennedy |website=[[Veja (magazine)|Veja]] |date=27 June 2011 |access-date=6 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://g1.globo.com/bahia/noticia/2013/07/para-celebrar-dia-g1-ensina-receita-facil-de-pizza-de-strogonoff-de-carne.html |title=Para celebrar dia, G1 ensina receita fácil de pizza de strogonoff de carne |first=Danutta |last=Rodrigues |website=[[G1 (website)|G1]] |date=10 July 2013 |access-date=6 September 2021}}</ref>

Sweet pizzas are also very common in Brazil, and usually fall into one of two main categories: [[chocolate pizza|chocolate]] or [[banana]]. Chocolate pizzas are more versatile in their ingredients, being topped with chocolate sprinkles to mimic a [[brigadeiro]], [[M&M's]], [[Strawberry|strawberries]] or sometimes [[Chocolate brownie|brownie]] chunks or even [[ice cream]]. Banana pizzas, on the other hand, are usually covered in [[sugar]] and [[cinnamon]], and sometimes have a layer of mozzarella beneath the bananas.<ref name="br-pizzaprime">{{cite web |url=https://www.pizzaprime.com.br/pizza-doce-sabores/ |title=Pizza doce: sabores para experimentar |language=pt-br |website=Blog Pizza Prime |date=21 November 2018 |access-date=6 September 2021}}</ref>

Stuffed crusts are also available for sweet pizzas: they can be stuffed with a variety of chocolates, or even [[Nutella|hazelnut and cocoa creams]].<ref name="br-pizzaprime" />

===Uruguay===
Popular varieties include ''pizza rellena'' (stuffed pizza), ''pizza por metro'' (pizza by the meter), and ''pizza a la parrilla'' (grilled pizza). While Uruguayan pizza largely derives from [[Neapolitan cuisine]], yeast-leavened Sicilian pizza is common on events such as birthdays or reunions under the name ''pizza de cumpleaños'' (birthday pizza). The ''figazza'' derives from [[focaccia#focaccia genovese|focaccia genovese]] ([[Republic of Genoa|Genoan]]) and consists of a thick pizza dough topped with onions and sometimes olives and/or bell peppers; less common is the addition of mozzarella on top of the onion layer.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://cocinacaseradeluruguay.wordpress.com/2020/11/29/pizza-y-faina/ | title=Pizza y Fainá | date=29 November 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JIlAEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22figazza%22&pg=PT103 | title=¿Qué es boniato, maestro? Pequeño diccionario ilustrado de uruguayismos para porteños: Contiene como chiquicientas definiciones | isbn=9789974872370 | last1=Rojas | first1=Gustavo Fripp | date=15 April 2020 | publisher=Alter ediciones }}</ref>
